I found five problems to fix before you use this file. None of them breaks it, but each one will skew results if you leave it alone. The dates are clean: no bad timestamps, and every day from 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30 is present (365 days).

Problems to fix:
- Product names are spelled inconsistently. There are 32 distinct values but really only 8 products. 800 rows use a different case ("latte", "LATTE") or have a trailing space ("Latte "), and the spaced versions look the same as the real names in the profile. If you don't trim spaces and standardise the case, product totals will come out too low.
- unit_price is stored as text ("$4.75"), so you need to strip the "$" and convert it to a number before doing any maths with it.
- There are 165 exact duplicate rows, about $788 of revenue. I'm fairly sure they're double exports: no other order ever has the same product on two separate lines, so these should be dropped.
- 492 rows (1.5%) have no store, spread evenly across all months. For 189 of them, another line in the same order has the store, so you can fill those in. The other 303 have no way to recover it.
- 133 rows have negative quantities (-1 to -3), worth -$671. These look like refunds, not errors. Keep them for net revenue and leave them out if you're counting units sold. Only 38% of them share an order_id with a sale, so most can't be matched back to the original purchase.

Things that are real but will distort comparisons:
- Prices went up on 2026-04-01: Latte from $4.75 to $5.25 and Cappuccino from $4.50 to $5.00. The other products have a single price all year, which makes unit_price consistent within each product and period.
- Matcha Latte first appears on 2026-03-01, so it only has 7 months of data. A full-year average or ranking will understate it, so compare it over the months it was on sale.
- Campus volume falls by about two thirds in June–August (around 270–370 rows a month, compared with 800–970 otherwise). This is probably the summer break, not missing data, but it will drag down Campus's annual averages.
- Sales shift towards cold drinks in summer: Cold Brew and Iced Latte go up while hot drinks go down. Keep that in mind when you compare months.

Checks that passed: within each order_id, store, timestamp, payment method and loyalty flag always agree. A repeated order_id just means an order with several items. Payment method and loyalty values are clean (card/app/cash, yes/no).

Overall these issues are small: the duplicates and refunds together are under 1% of the $164,732 gross revenue. The name spelling and price-as-text problems are the ones that will give wrong answers if you don't fix them. If you want, I can apply all these fixes and hand back a cleaned DataFrame.

prompt: Before I use this data, are there any quality problems I should know about?

meta.answer:

All of them can be fixed, but they will skew results if you use the file as-is.** Overall the data looks complete: there are no unparseable timestamps, every day from 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30 has data, and each order_id always has one timestamp, payment method and loyalty flag.

- **Product names are inconsistent.** There are 32 names for only 8 products. The differences are capitalization ("latte", "LATTE") and a trailing space ("Latte "). About 870 rows are affected. If you group without cleaning, each product will be split into several pieces. Trimming spaces and fixing the capitalization fixes it.
- **Prices are stored as text** ("$4.75"). You need to remove the "$" and convert them to numbers before doing any math.
- **There are 165 exact duplicate rows.** The order, timestamp, store, product, quantity and price are all identical. They are most likely double-loaded lines, and together they add $787.75 of revenue. I can't prove they aren't real repeat lines, but I'd remove them.
- **492 rows (1.5%) have no store.** 189 of these belong to orders where other lines do list a store, so you can fill them in from those lines. The other 303 can't be assigned to a store.
- **There are 133 refund lines** with quantity -1 to -3, worth -$671.25. None of them sit in the same order as a sale of that product, so you can't match a refund to its original purchase. Count them as negative revenue, but leave them out of "units sold" or "number of sales" figures.

Things that are real but can mislead comparisons:
- **Prices went up on 2026-04-01.** Cappuccino went from $4.50 to $5.00 and Latte from $4.75 to $5.25. Part of any revenue growth after April is price, not volume.
- **Matcha Latte only started on 2026-03-01.** If you average it over all 12 months, you'll understate it by almost half. Use only the 7 months it was on sale.
- **Campus sales drop from June to August 2026**, to about 270–370 rows a month compared with about 800–970 normally. Downtown and Riverside stay flat, so this looks like a summer break rather than missing data. Keep it in mind when comparing stores or months.

Fine as-is: order_id repeats are just orders with several items (26,554 orders across 33,237 lines). Payment method and loyalty values are clean.
